title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting, representative validator-trace excerpts, quantitative analysis, failure-mode diagnostics, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps workflows with generative models requires reliable mechanisms to avoid harmful, silent, or wrong-but-plausible actions. A common operational pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): a generator (LLM) proposes a candidate configuration or plan, a deterministic validator mechanically checks correctness and policy constraints, and when necessary a repair module synthesizes corrected candidates or triggers human review. Prior demonstrations of GVR-like architectures in code and system domains motivate their adoption in NetOps, but systematic, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (false-positive/false-negative rates), detection latency, and predictive usefulness for end-to-end guarded success are scarce.

We preregistered study AC-2026-03 with a paired design that isolates the effect of downstream validator-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each task the generator produced a single initial candidate that was reused by both the baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator + permitted repair) conditions. Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise downstream from validator-triggered repair, not from independent generator sampling. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (H1) expected that a multidimensional validator-metric suite would explain more variance in end-to-end success than a single verifier pass rate. Our main contribution here is a fully preregistered, artifact-archived experiment and an exact, transparent report of a degenerate confirmatory outcome (ceiling) with concrete, artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up designs that can measure validator utility.
sections.related_work:
Architectural and system reports have advocated GVR and tool-augmented verifier layers for reducing stochastic generator errors and enabling deterministic acceptance criteria [1]. Benchmarks for AIOps and NetOps document operational failure modes—ticket noise, false premises, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that motivate such verifier insertions [2],[3]. Prototype reports describe self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair that reduce silent or action-triggering failures in controlled evaluations [4]. Broad surveys of LLMs for telecommunications and NetOps summarize adaptation and verification trade-offs and motivate measuring verification cost alongside nominal correctness [5].

Collectively these works justify careful measurement of validator soundness and operational impact but do not deliver a standardized, empirically estimable validator-metric suite tailored to NetOps GVR flows. Our preregistered study was designed to begin filling that measurement gap under strict preregistration and archived-execution practices. We treat prior demonstrations as architectural and motivational evidence rather than as establishing empirical coverage for NetOps validators; we do not extrapolate beyond the supplied records.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key preregistered elements (recorded in the preregistration manifest): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini via provider bundle 'openai_responses'; task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false (explicit). The preregistration included a power plan targeting detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 at α = 0.05 with ~80% power under conservative assumptions; bootstrap stability checks were specified for planning and the analysis executor used 10,000 resamples with seed 1729 as archived.

Task bank and deterministic task selection. Tasks were drawn deterministically from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) at difficulty levels labelled 'very_hard' and 'extreme'. Each task encodes: an initial_state, an expected_final_state, a compact intent, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields), and a required_command_sequence. Task selection followed the preregistered deterministic index rule (challenging_workflow_stress_v1). Contamination controls (exact SHA-256 duplicate exclusion and semantic-similarity exclusion at cosine > 0.95) were preregistered; no exclusions occurred (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty).

Model and provider configuration. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair) and maximum_model_calls = 400 as preregistered. Important artifact-grounded note: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider-side sampling variability may still exist and all provider-call audit fields are recorded in the execution manifest.

Validator, scoring, and success label. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator performs mechanistic intent-constraint checks and emits per-episode fields: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair artifacts when repairs are invoked. The preregistered binary scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) uses validator.valid as the success label for the confirmatory estimand. The pipeline permitted at most one repair call when validator rejected a candidate; repairs would be recorded in repair_provider_trace fields and repair_applied toggled accordingly.

Execution controls, missingness, and exclusions. The preregistered maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries). The confirmatory analysis plan required complete pairs; sensitivity analyses were prespecified to treat missing episodes as failures. The execution manifest reports completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, and complete_pair_count = 200. All raw responses, provider-call traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts were archived in the execution bundle and are referenced in this manuscript.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The adapter completed the preregistered run with planned_episode_count = 400 and completed_episode_count = 400. Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. In short, exactly one shared initial generation was sampled per task and reused for the paired baseline and guarded episodes as preregistered.

Primary confirmatory outcome. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Analysis artifacts state baseline_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test (predeclared) yields p = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. These numeric results are archived in analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and match the confirmed analysis log (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).

Representative validator-trace excerpt (artifact-grounded). A compact excerpt from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json illustrates per-episode validator fields verbatim from the archive:

  pair_id: pair-000004
  normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  parsed_command_count: 4
  required_command_count: 4
  observed_touched_field_count: 3
  valid: true
  repair_applied: false
  validator_id: deterministic_netops_validator_v5
  validator_version: 5.0

For this exemplar the parsed/required command counts match, no violation codes were emitted, and the validator did not request repair. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode.

Exploratory diagnostics and null structure. Because baseline and guarded evaluated the identical shared initial candidate per pair, any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair. The observed all-valid outcome therefore produced a degenerate paired distribution with zero discordant pairs (n_10 = n_01 = 0). This degeneracy renders the preplanned power calculation (targeting a 0.10 absolute paired improvement) inapplicable for the observed data: when baseline success = 1.0 the paired-estimator variance is zero and no test can detect an improvement that cannot occur on the observed data.

Archival artifact references. The execution bundle contains the full raw results (execution/raw_results.jsonl), per-episode scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl), model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json), analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg), the preregistration manifest (preregistration_sha256 recorded), and the initial master-prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256). These artifacts permit exact reproduction of the numeric summaries reported above.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the degenerate outcome. The paired shared_initial_candidate semantics precisely isolate downstream validator-triggered repair effects but also concentrate risk of a single-sample ceiling when the generator and validator align. In this execution three artifact-grounded factors explain the ceiling: (1) the synthetic generator produced structurally valid candidates for every sampled seed in the deterministic task index; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling plan eliminated generator variability as a potential source of discordant outcomes; and (3) the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic checks and does not reveal semantic intent misalignment when candidates are correct-by-structure. The artifacts (validator_trace.valid = true, repair_applied = false for every episode) substantiate each factor.

Operational implications and scope. These results do not imply that validators are unnecessary in general. Rather, they demonstrate that for this synthetic bank, model seeds, and validator implementation there were zero detectable mechanical defects to catch. Deterministic validators will be effective only insofar as the task bank and generator produce mechanically detectable defects. For real-world operational settings, semantic misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent) is an important failure mode that mechanistic validators may not detect without additional intent-grounding signals, operator feedback, or richer specification channels.

Artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered arms. The archived adapter semantics and artifacts support concrete, preregistered follow-up arms to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair utility without manual artifact edits: (A) a fault-injection arm that deterministically injects syntactic, configuration-logic, and semantic-intent faults into reference answers for a fraction f of tasks; (B) a multi-sample generation arm with initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws per task to reveal generator variability and create opportunities for validator rejection and repair; (C) a multi-validator and multi-model arm that adds an alternative validator implementation and at least one additional model family to quantify validator-design sensitivity and external validity. Each prescription is implementable using the archived deterministic task generator, contamination rules, and adapter semantics and does not contradict preregistered controls.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics deliberately isolates downstream effects but introduced single-sample ceiling risk. Construct validity: the binary label validator.valid operationalizes mechanistic correctness but may fail to capture semantic intent alignment required by operators. External validity: a synthetic task bank, one model (gpt-5-mini), and one deterministic validator limit generalization to heterogeneous production networks. Conclusion validity: the degenerate outcome produced zero variance in the primary estimand; hence inferential conclusions about validator benefit are not possible from this execution alone. These limitations are recorded in the execution and analysis artifacts and motivate the artifact-grounded follow-up arms above.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, the sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. This result is artifact-grounded and reproducible from the archived bundle. We publish the exact execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and provide concrete, preregistered experiment prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) that are required to produce estimable validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions. The artifacts and analysis logs are archived in the execution bundle for community reanalysis and for use as the basis of follow-up preregistered experiments that can resolve the open measurement questions identified here.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
